claims.text: As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy films or nanoribbons have a nanocrystalline or textured microstructure typical of physical-vapor deposition.
Restricted dimensions confine magnetic-domain nucleation in these films and nanoribbons.
Restricted dimensions produce inhomogeneous strain fields.
Confined domain nucleation and inhomogeneous strain slow the kinetics of a field-driven phase transformation.
Strong substrate coupling limits thermal equilibration during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Nanoscale grains and interface-dominated thermal paths create a nonuniform internal temperature distribution during cooling.
The nonuniform internal temperature distribution confines magnetic-domain nucleation and phase transformation to limited regions of the film.
Reduced dimensionality and substrate thermal coupling generate thermal gradients and delays in heat extraction.
Thermal gradients and delayed heat extraction impede completion of the magnetic phase transformation during each cooling cycle.
An incomplete magnetic phase transformation increases hysteresis.
An incomplete magnetic phase transformation reduces the magnetocaloric response relative to bulk samples.
Adding a thin Au or Cu interlayer between the alloy and substrate enhances interfacial heat transfer.
Enhanced interfacial heat transfer permits a faster approach to thermal equilibrium during each cycle.
Enhanced interfacial heat transfer allows the magnetic phase transition to proceed more completely.
Relative to samples without an interlayer, samples with enhanced interfacial heat transfer will exhibit narrower magnetic hysteresis loops.

Relative to samples without an interlayer, samples with enhanced interfacial heat transfer will exhibit a larger and more recoverable magnetocaloric temperature change under the same low-field conditions.
The proposed effect is expected under applied fields below 0.5 T and cycle frequencies of approximately 0.1–5 Hz.
At higher fields or for thicker, more bulk-like films, the difference caused by the thermal interlayer may diminish.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes poor equilibration to 'strong substrate coupling' and the mechanism similarly invokes 'strong substrate thermal coupling' as a cause of delayed heat extraction, while the intervention proposes increasing interfacial thermal coupling/conductivity to improve equilibration. Mechanical coupling and thermal resistance may have been conflated, leaving the stated direction of substrate coupling internally inconsistent.
